title: Pixel Loom
tagline: A little world, one pixel at a time.
description: A local-first pixel-art and flipbook editor. Draw on transparent layers, animate small sprites, and export PNG frames or sprite sheets.
projectNotes: Inspired by Aseprite’s pixel-art and animation workflow. This is an independent learning project, not an official Aseprite app or a claim of feature-for-feature compatibility.
Editable projects use Pixel Loom’s own JSON format. Aseprite project files, GIF/APNG export, selections, and variable frame timing are not supported.
Create canvases up to 128 × 128 pixels with up to 12 layers and 32 frames, within a total limit of two million stored cells.
Artwork stays in your browser. Download editable project backups for important work; browser autosave is best effort and can be lost if storage is cleared.

title: Kata Orbitweave
description: A procedural motion playground using 3D coordinates and Canvas 2D orthographic projection. Arrange clones, combine effectors, and export a still or editable composition.
projectNotes: Inspired by Cinema 4D. Original independent educational kata, without affiliation, endorsement or proprietary file compatibility.

A Canvas 2D orthographic rendering of a 3D-coordinate scene, not WebGL or a full 3D modeler. Depth sorting can show intersection artifacts. No mesh import, physics, editable keyframes, native C4D files or video export.
Work stays in your browser. Autosave is best effort; download editable project backups. Undo history does not survive reload. Narrow-layout checks use desktop-browser iframes, not physical phones.
